title: Found Unconscious
hpi_narrative: A 40-year-old male is found unconscious with Carbon Monoxide Poisoning. Onset was sudden upon entering a burning building. Associated symptoms include potential neurological deficits, severe lung damage, and possible cardiac ischemia.

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Carbon Monoxide poisoning can cause cardiac ischemia
physical_exam.respiratory: The patient was found in a burning building filled with smoke. The patient could have severe lung damage

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: Patient unconscious — appropriate to look at patient's general appearance.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych
stacks.finding: As the patient presented unconscious, a neuro exam should be done to evaluate the patient's neurological status.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs
stacks.finding: The patient was found in a burning building filled with smoke. The patient could have severe lung damage, so this should be evaluated.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular
stacks.finding: Carbon Monoxide poisoning can cause cardiac ischemia, so a cardiac exam should be done.

stacks.label: Arterial blood gases
stacks.finding: ABG is important to determine the acid/base status. This will show a primary respiratory acidosis with secondary metabolic acidosis.

stacks.label: Lactate, serum
stacks.finding: Lactate aids in differentiating between cyanide poisoning and carbon monoxide poisoning. If lactate is normal or mildly elevated, then this would be more consistent with carbon monoxide poisoning alone.

stacks.label: Carbon monoxide, blood
stacks.finding: The patient was found in a burning building. Carbon Monoxide poisoning is high on the differential. This should be checked.
